summary: dateuuidv2 executes obfuscated remote payload on require()
details: The package advertises itself as a UUIDv7 utility but on require() runs lib/bootstrap.js, which reconstructs a remote URL by AES-256-GCM-decrypting a hardcoded ciphertext patched with characters read from a PORT= line in the installer's README.md, POSTs os.platform() and os.release() to that URL, writes the response body to %TEMP%/temp_<timestamp>.vbs (extension assembled as '.v'+'b'+'s' to evade scanners), and executes it via child_process.exec. The dropper flow is entirely unrelated to the advertised UUID functionality, uses runtime-decrypted destinations, and exfiltrates host OS fingerprinting as part of the handshake.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
